intro: Prefixes and endings that let you understand, and make, words you have never seen.
p.deshacer.consejo: The prefix «des-» reverses the idea: «hacer» and «deshacer». The h is silent.
p.desordenado.consejo: It comes from «ordenado» plus «des-». It is an adjective: «una habitación desordenada».
p.increíble.consejo: It comes from «creer». «In-» means «not» and the ending «-ible» means «that can be».
p.imposible.consejo: It is «posible» with «in-», but before p it is written «im-». Never «inposible».
p.rehacer.consejo: The prefix «re-» means «again»: «releer», «rehacer». The h is silent: «rre-a-THER».
p.felicidad.consejo: It comes from «feliz». The z becomes c before «i»: «feliz», «felicidad». It ends in «-dad»: feminine.
p.información.consejo: It comes from «informar». Nouns in «-ción» are always feminine: «la información».
p.conocimiento.consejo: It comes from «conocer». The ending «-miento» gives masculine nouns: «el conocimiento».
p.belleza.consejo: It comes from «bello». The ending «-eza» forms feminine quality nouns: «belleza», «tristeza».
p.amable.consejo: It comes from «amar»: «-able» means «that can be». So «amable» is «worthy of love».
p.peligroso.consejo: It comes from «peligro». The ending «-oso» means «full of»: «peligroso», «famoso».
p.trabajador.consejo: It comes from «trabajar». The ending «-dor» gives adjectives and nouns for people: «trabajador».
p.panadería.consejo: It comes from «pan». The ending «-ería» names shops: «panadería», «frutería». The í has a tilde.
b1.texto:
**Prefixes** change the meaning of a word.

- **des-** undoes or reverses: hacer → **des**hacer, ordenado → **des**ordenado.
- **in-, im-, i-** mean «not»: posible → **im**posible, legal → **i**legal.
- **re-** means «again»: hacer → **re**hacer, leer → **re**leer.

**Endings** change the kind of word.

- Nouns: informar → la informa**ción**; feliz → la felici**dad**; conocer → el conoci**miento**; bello → la bell**eza**.
- Adjectives: amar → am**able**; creer → cre**íble**; peligro → peligr**oso**; trabajar → trabaja**dor**.
- Shops and trades: pan → la panad**ería**, el panad**ero**.

The ending also gives you the gender: **-ción, -sión, -dad, -tad, -tud** are feminine; **-miento, -aje, -or** are masculine.
b2.f1.texto: It is impossible to tidy it in five minutes.
b2.f2.texto: Happiness starts with a made bed.
b2.f3.texto: Does that information come from some book?
b2.f4.texto: It is a very old piece of popular wisdom.
b2.f5.texto: I will remake the bed and then go down to the bakery.
b2.f6.texto: The baker on the corner is kind and hard-working.
b2.f7.texto: That freshly baked bread is incredible.
b4.titulo: How a derived word is formed
b4.texto:
A derived word has a **root** and one or two added pieces.

- **Prefix + root**: **des**+hacer, **im**+posible, **re**+hacer. The prefix goes first and does not change the kind of word.
- **Root + suffix**: peligro+**oso**, bell+**eza**, informa+**ción**. The suffix goes after and almost always changes the kind of word.
- **Spelling**: «in-» is written **im-** before p and b (**im**posible, **im**borrable); the z of «feliz» becomes c (felici**dad**).
- **Gender**: the suffix decides. If you see **-ción** or **-dad**, the noun is **feminine**; if you see **-miento**, it is **masculine**.

With this method you understand a new word before opening the dictionary.
b4.e0.texto: With time we can redo any plan.
b4.e1.texto: The beauty of the landscape is incredible.
b5.f0.texto: An old bakery occupies the corner of the narrow street.
b5.f1.texto: The lit oven fills the air with a sweet, thick perfume.
b5.f2.texto: The wooden shelves hold loaves of every shape.
b5.f3.texto: A hard-working baker kneads the flour from before dawn.
b5.f4.texto: His hands, white with flour, shape each loaf.
b5.f5.texto: A kind neighbour comes in through the door with a cloth bag.
b5.f6.texto: The wet floor looks dangerous on rainy days.
b5.f7.texto: The woman smiles at the baker with a gesture of happiness.
b5.f8.texto: Each loaf carries inside it the knowledge of many years.
b5.f9.texto: The whole bakery smells of fresh bread and of home.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Well done: «in-» is written «im-» before p.
b6.o1.refuerzo: Before p the prefix is «im-», not «in-».
b6.o2.refuerzo: «Des-» goes with verbs and participles, not with «posible».
b7.o0.refuerzo: That is the adverb: «happily». A noun is missing here.
b7.o2.refuerzo: A «felicitación» is a congratulation, not a state.
b8.o2.refuerzo: That is it: all nouns in «-ción» are feminine.
b8.pregunta: Which ending tells you a noun is feminine?
b9.o1.refuerzo: «Des-» undoes it; it does not repeat it.
b9.o2.refuerzo: «Pre-» means «before», and that verb does not exist.
b10.frase: Rehago la cama antes de desayunar
b10.traduccion: I remake the bed before having breakfast
b11.pregunta: Write the opposite of «ordenado» using a prefix.
b12.o0.refuerzo: El panadero is the person. The shop takes «-ería».
b12.o1.refuerzo: Very good: «-ería» names the place where it is sold.
b12.o2.refuerzo: La panera is the basket where bread is kept at home.
p.completamente.consejo: Add «-mente» to the adjective «completa» to make an adverb, like «totalmente».
p.desordenada.consejo: The prefix «des-» reverses the idea: «ordenada» becomes «desordenada», the opposite.
p.ordenarla.consejo: Two parts: the verb «ordenar» and the pronoun «la», meaning «it» for a feminine noun.
p.popular.consejo: Very close to English, but the Spanish «p» is softer and the «r» is a single tap.
p.rehago.consejo: From «hacer», with «re-» meaning again. The h is silent: «re-A-go».
p.crea.consejo: From «crear», to create. The vowels «e» and «a» are pronounced in separate syllables.
p.espeso.consejo: Think of a thick soup, «espeso»: the stress falls on the second syllable, «PE».
p.estanterías.consejo: Plural of «estantería». The accent on the «í» stays in the plural form.
p.guardan.consejo: From «guardar», to keep. The «u» is pronounced because the next vowel is «a».
p.panes.consejo: Plural of «pan», bread. Words ending in a consonant add «-es» in the plural.
p.formas.consejo: The «r» sits between vowels, so it is a soft single tap: «FOR-mas».
p.amasa.consejo: From «masa», dough. The verb means to knead dough with the hands.
p.gesto.consejo: The «g» before «e» sounds like a soft English «h»: «HES-to», stressed on the first syllable.
p.hogar.consejo: The «h» is silent, so you hear «o-GAR», with the stress on the last syllable.
p.ción.consejo: A suffix that turns many verbs into nouns. In «información» it is written with a «c».
p.rehacerlo.consejo: The verb «rehacer» plus «lo» (it, masculine). The pronoun joins the end of the verb.
